desc: Design algorithm: sort A, B, C descending so F(i,j,k)=A_iB_j+B_jC_k+C_kA_i is monotone nonincreasing in each index; K ≤ 5×10^5 makes best-first heap extraction feasible while O(N^2) counting for binary search is not.

Establish correctness invariant: tree expansion (parent = decrement leftmost nonzero coordinate) gives each node exactly one parent with value ≥ its own, so heap pops yield values in nonincreasing order and the K-th pop is the K-th largest, duplicates included.
Implement complete Python solution: fast input, descending sorts, packed-int heap keys `((-value)<<53)|code`, tree-based best-first from (0,0,0) with no visited set, print K-th popped value.

Verify edge cases and performance: packing is lossless (value < 2^62, code < 2^53; arithmetic shift/mask decode exactly, and value dominates heap order since code < 2^53); traced Sample 1 manually — pops are 44, 38, 36, 34, 31, so 5th = 31 ✓; all-equal arrays give identical values with correct duplicate counting (Sample 2); N=1/K=1 terminates after root pop with no pushes; heap never empties early since total nodes N^3 ≥ K; ~2×10^6 heap operations at K=5×10^5 runs in a few seconds and heap memory (~2K packed ints ≈ 40MB) is within typical limits.
